qe: मुंह में लार के साथ मिले हुए भोजन को ____ कहा जाता है।
qh: The food mixed with saliva in the mouth is called ____.
e: Once food is chewed and mixed with saliva, it is referred to as a bolus. / एक बार जब भोजन चबाया जाता है और लार के साथ मिल जाता है, तो उसे बोलस कहा जाता है।

qe: लार में कौन सा एंजाइम भोजन के साथ प्रवेश करने वाले बैक्टीरिया को मारता है?
qh: Which enzyme in saliva kills bacteria entering with food?
e: Lysozyme acts as an antibacterial agent in saliva. / लाइसोजाइम लार में एक जीवाणुरोधी एजेंट के रूप में कार्य करता है।

qe: मानव लार में कौन से एंजाइम 'स्टार्च' (चोकर) के पाचन में मदद करते हैं?
qh: Which enzymes in human saliva help in the digestion of 'Starch' (Chokar)?
o: Tyline and Diastase | टायलिन और डायस्टेज
e: Tyline and Diastase break down starch/carbohydrates in the mouth. / टायलिन और डायस्टेज मुंह में स्टार्च/कार्बोहाइड्रेट को तोड़ते हैं।

qe: लार में 'म्यूलिन' का क्या कार्य है?
qh: What is the function of 'Mylin' (Mucus) in saliva?
o: Make food sticky and easy to swallow | भोजन को चिपचिपा बनाना
e: Mylin lubricates food so it can easily slide down the esophagus. / म्यूलिन भोजन को चिकना बनाता है ताकि वह आसानी से ग्रास नली से नीचे जा सके।

qe: मानव शरीर में सबसे बड़ी 'लार ग्रंथि' कौन सी है?
qh: Which is the largest 'Salivary Gland' in the human body?
e: The parotid gland is the largest salivary gland. In snakes, it often contains venom. / पैरोटिड ग्रंथि सबसे बड़ी लार ग्रंथि है। सांपों में, इसमें अक्सर जहर होता है।

qe: आहार नाल के किस भाग में कोई पाचन नहीं होता है?
qh: In which part of the Alimentary Canal does NO digestion occur?
e: The esophagus only transports food to the stomach via peristalsis. / ग्रास नली केवल क्रमानुकुंचन के माध्यम से भोजन को आमाशय तक पहुँचाती है।

qe: वह लहर जैसी गति जो भोजन को ग्रास नली से नीचे धकेलती है, ____ कहलाती है।
qh: The wave-like movement that pushes food down the esophagus is called ____.
e: Peristalsis is the rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscles to move food. / क्रमानुकुंचन भोजन को स्थानांतरित करने के लिए मांसपेशियों का लयबद्ध संकुचन और शिथिलन है।

qe: एक वयस्क मानव द्वारा प्रतिदिन लगभग कितनी लार स्रावित होती है?
qh: Approximately how much saliva is secreted daily by an adult human?
e: The average adult secretes between 1 to 1.5 liters of saliva per day. / औसत वयस्क प्रतिदिन 1 से 1.5 लीटर लार स्रावित करता है।

qe: आहार नाल का कौन सा भाग अनपचे भोजन को मल के रूप में संचित करता है?
qh: Which part of the Alimentary Canal stores undigested food as feces?
e: Fecal matter is stored in the rectum before elimination. / मल त्याग से पहले मलाशय में जमा होता है।

qe: मनुष्य कच्ची घास/लकड़ी को आसानी से पचाने में क्यों विफल रहते हैं?
qh: Why do humans fail to digest raw grass/wood easily?
o: Lack of cellulose-digesting bacteria | सेलुलोज पचाने वाले बैक्टीरिया की कमी
e: Humans cannot digest cellulose as we lack the specific bacteria found in herbivores. / मनुष्य सेलुलोज को नहीं पचा सकते क्योंकि हममें शाकाहारी जीवों में पाए जाने वाले विशिष्ट बैक्टीरिया की कमी होती है।

qe: मानव शरीर में पाचन का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है?
qh: What is the primary purpose of digestion in the human body?
o: To convert complex substances into Glucose | जटिल पदार्थों को ग्लूकोज में बदलना
e: Digestion breaks down complex food items like carbohydrates into simpler forms like glucose for energy. / पाचन ऊर्जा के लिए कार्बोहाइड्रेट जैसे जटिल खाद्य पदार्थों को ग्लूकोज जैसे सरल रूपों में तोड़ता है।

qe: मनुष्यों में पाचन की प्रक्रिया कहाँ से शुरू होती है?
qh: Where does the process of digestion start in humans?
e: Digestion begins in the mouth with the mechanical breakdown of food by teeth and chemical action of saliva. / पाचन मुंह में दांतों द्वारा भोजन के यांत्रिक विखंडन और लार की रासायनिक क्रिया से शुरू होता है।

qe: मानव 'आहार नाल' की अनुमानित लंबाई कितनी होती है?
qh: What is the approximate length of the human 'Alimentary Canal'?
e: The alimentary canal is a long tube-like structure about 32 feet or 9 meters long. / आहार नाल एक लंबी नली जैसी संरचना है जो लगभग 32 फीट या 9 मीटर लंबी होती है।

qe: पाचन तंत्र का कौन सा भाग भोजन के लिए एक सामान्य मार्ग है लेकिन इसमें कोई पाचन नहीं होता है?
qh: Which part of the digestive system is a common passage for food but has NO digestion occurring in it?
e: The esophagus only transports food from the mouth to the stomach via peristalsis. / ग्रास नली केवल क्रमानुकुंचन के माध्यम से भोजन को मुंह से आमाशय तक पहुँचाती है।

qe: ग्रास नली में भोजन की गति के लिए जैविक शब्द क्या है?
qh: What is the biological term for the movement of food down the esophagus?
e: Peristalsis is the wave-like muscle contraction that moves food through the digestive tract. / क्रमानुकुंचन लहर जैसी मांसपेशियों का संकुचन है जो भोजन को पाचन मार्ग से ले जाता है।

qe: आहार नाल के क्रम में 'आमाशय' (पेट) कहाँ स्थित होता है?
qh: Where is the 'Stomach' located in the sequence of the Alimentary Canal?
o: After Esophagus | ग्रास नली के बाद
e: Food travels from the mouth through the esophagus into the stomach (Amashay). / भोजन मुंह से ग्रास नली के माध्यम से आमाशय (Amashay) में जाता है।

qe: भोजन का अधिकांश पाचन और अवशोषण कहाँ होता है?
qh: Where does most of the digestion and absorption of food take place?
e: The small intestine is the primary site for chemical digestion and nutrient absorption. / छोटी आंत रासायनिक पाचन और पोषक तत्वों के अवशोषण का प्राथमिक स्थल है।

qe: 'मलाशय' (Rectum) में क्या संचित होता है?
qh: What is stored in the 'Rectum' (मलाशय)?
e: The rectum stores solid waste until it is expelled through the anus. / मलाशय ठोस अपशिष्ट को तब तक संचित करता है जब तक कि उसे गुदा के माध्यम से बाहर न निकाल दिया जाए।

qe: एक औसत मनुष्य एक दिन में कितनी लार (Saliva) पैदा करता है?
qh: How much saliva does an average human produce in a day?
e: An adult human typically secretes around 1 to 1.5 liters of saliva daily. / एक वयस्क मनुष्य आमतौर पर प्रतिदिन लगभग 1 से 1.5 लीटर लार स्रावित करता है।

qe: लार में कौन सा एंजाइम भोजन में बैक्टीरिया को मारकर प्राकृतिक 'सैनिटाइजर' के रूप में कार्य करता है?
qh: Which enzyme in saliva acts as a natural 'Sanitizer' by killing bacteria in food?
e: Lysozyme in saliva kills many of the bacteria that enter the mouth with food. / लार में मौजूद लाइसोजाइम भोजन के साथ मुंह में प्रवेश करने वाले कई बैक्टीरिया को मार देता है।

qe: 'अग्नाशय' को जीव विज्ञान में किस नाम से जाना जाता है?
qh: The 'Pancreas' is biologically known as ____ in Hindi.
e: Pancreas is called Agnashay, while Stomach is called Amashay. / पैंक्रियाज को अग्नाशय कहा जाता है, जबकि स्टमक को आमाशय कहा जाता है।

qe: इनमें से कौन आहार नाल के मार्ग का हिस्सा नहीं है?
qh: Which of these is NOT a part of the Alimentary Canal path?
e: Liver is a digestive gland, not a tube that food passes through. / लीवर एक पाचन ग्रंथि है, न कि वह नली जिससे भोजन गुजरता है।

qe: 'मुख गुहा' (Buccal Cavity) का तात्पर्य किससे है?
qh: The term 'Buccal Cavity' refers to ____.
e: Buccal cavity is the empty space in the mouth where food is first received. / मुख गुहा मुंह का वह खाली स्थान है जहां भोजन सबसे पहले प्राप्त होता है।

qe: शिशुओं को हिचकी अधिक बार क्यों आती है?
qh: Why do infants get hiccups more frequently according ?
o: Their brain is still learning to coordinate swallowing | मस्तिष्क का तालमेल अभी विकसित हो रहा है
e: Infants' brains are not yet fully habituated to separating respiratory and digestive signals. / शिशुओं का मस्तिष्क अभी तक श्वसन और पाचन संकेतों को अलग करने का पूरी तरह अभ्यस्त नहीं हुआ है।

qe: टायलिन और डायस्टेज जैसे एंजाइमों को स्रावित करने के लिए कौन सी ग्रंथि जिम्मेदार है?
qh: Which gland is responsible for secreting enzymes like Ptyalin and Diastase?
e: Salivary glands secrete enzymes that begin the digestion of starch. / लार ग्रंथियां उन एंजाइमों को स्रावित करती हैं जो स्टार्च का पाचन शुरू करते हैं।

qe: 'बड़ी आंत', 'छोटी आंत' की तुलना में ____ होती है।
qh: The 'Large Intestine' is ____ than the 'Small Intestine'.
o: Shorter but wider | छोटी लेकिन चौड़ी
e: The large intestine has a larger diameter but is much shorter in length than the small intestine. / बड़ी आंत का व्यास बड़ा होता है लेकिन लंबाई में यह छोटी आंत से काफी छोटी होती है।

qe: आहार नाल के किस भाग में अनपचा भोजन मल के रूप में संचित होता है?
qh: In which part of the alimentary canal is undigested food stored as feces?
e: The rectum is the final section of the large intestine where feces is stored. / मलाशय बड़ी आंत का अंतिम भाग है जहां मल जमा होता है।

qe: कौन सा अंग लैक्टिक एसिड को वापस ग्लूकोज/ग्लाइकोजन में बदल देता है?
qh: Which organ converts lactic acid back into glucose/glycogen?
e: The liver processes lactic acid to recover energy. / लीवर ऊर्जा की रिकवरी के लिए लैक्टिक एसिड को संसाधित करता है।

qe: पेट के अंदर हमारे द्वारा पिए गए दूध को दही में कौन सा एंजाइम/अंग बदलता है?
qh: Which organ converts the milk we drink into curd (yogurt) inside the stomach?
e: Renin is responsible for the coagulation of milk in infants and adults. / रेनिन शिशुओं और वयस्कों में दूध के जमने के लिए जिम्मेदार है।

qe: मानव शरीर का कौन सा अंग क्षतिग्रस्त होने पर भी पूरी तरह से पुनर्जीवित हो सकता है?
qh: Which organ in the human body can fully regenerate even if damaged?
e: The liver has the highest capacity for cell division and regeneration. / लीवर में कोशिका विभाजन और पुनर्योजन की उच्चतम क्षमता होती है।

qe: मानव शरीर के किस अंग में पुनर्योजन (Regeneration) की शक्ति सबसे अधिक होती है?
qh: Which organ in the human body has the highest power of regeneration?
e: The liver is the only organ in the human body that can regrow completely from a small part. / लीवर मानव शरीर का एकमात्र अंग है जो एक छोटे से हिस्से से पूरी तरह से दोबारा बढ़ सकता है।

qe: क्या मनुष्य 'सेलुलोज' को पचा सकते हैं?
qh: Can humans digest 'Cellulose'?
e: Humans lack the necessary bacteria and enzymes to break down tough cellulose. / मनुष्यों में कठोर सेलुलोज को तोड़ने के लिए आवश्यक बैक्टीरिया और एंजाइम नहीं होते हैं।

qe: कौन सा सबसे बड़ा आंतरिक अंग है जहाँ 'कोशिका विभाजन' बहुत तेज होता है?
qh: Which is the largest internal organ where 'Cell Division' is very fast?
e: The liver can regenerate even if a large part is removed. / लीवर का एक बड़ा हिस्सा हटा दिए जाने पर भी वह पुनर्योजन कर सकता है।

qe: मानव शरीर में सबसे तेजी से 'कोशिका विभाजन' कहाँ होता है?
qh: Where does the fastest 'Cell Division' occur in the human body?
e: The liver has a high regenerative capacity due to fast cell division. / तेज कोशिका विभाजन के कारण लीवर में पुनर्योजन की उच्च क्षमता होती है।

qe: Which organ in the human body has the highest power of regeneration?
e: The Liver is the only internal human organ that can regenerate itself completely.

qe: Protein digestion starts in which part of the digestive tract?
e: Pepsin enzyme in the stomach starts the breakdown of proteins.

qe: Which acid is present in the human stomach to help digestion?
e: HCl kills bacteria and creates an acidic environment for enzymes.

qe: Emulsification of fats is done by which substance?
e: Bile juice breaks down large fat globules into smaller droplets.

qe: The longest part of the human digestive system is:
e: The small intestine is about 6-7 meters long, though narrow in diameter.

qe: The yellow color of human feces is due to which pigment?
e: Bilirubin is a byproduct of red blood cell breakdown excreted in bile.

qe: Which part of the digestive system absorbs water and minerals from undigested food?
e: The primary function of the large intestine is to absorb water, salts, and some vitamins from the remaining indigestible food matter.

qe: In Jaundice, which organ is primarily affected?
e: Jaundice is caused by the buildup of bilirubin in the blood, indicating that the liver is not filtering blood properly.

qe: Which of the following prevents the entry of food into the windpipe (trachea)?
e: The epiglottis is a flap of cartilage that flips down during swallowing to cover the opening of the windpipe.

qe: Vitamins are absorbed primarily in which part of the small intestine?
e: While digestion starts in the duodenum, the final absorption of Vitamin B12 and bile salts happens in the Ileum.

qe: Which disorder is characterized by the inflammation of the liver?
e: 'Hepa' refers to the liver. Hepatitis is the inflammation of liver tissue, often caused by viruses.

qe: The semi-solid mass of food formed in the stomach is called:
e: Food mixed with gastric juices in the stomach is called Chyme. (Bolus is in the mouth; Chyle is in the small intestine).

qe: Which enzyme converts proteins into Peptones in the stomach?
e: Pepsin is secreted in an inactive form (pepsinogen) and becomes active in the presence of HCl to break down proteins.

qe: The 'Lacteals' in the small intestine are responsible for the absorption of:
e: Lacteals are lymphatic capillaries that absorb dietary fats in the villi of the small intestine.

qe: Which part of the Large Intestine hosts symbiotic bacteria?
e: The cecum is a small blind sac which hosts certain symbiotic micro-organisms that help in digestion.

qe: Protein deficiency in children leads to which disease?
e: Kwashiorkor is severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema (swelling) and an enlarged liver.

qe: In Jaundice, which organ is primarily affected due to the buildup of bilirubin?
e: Jaundice indicates a malfunction of the liver, where it fails to filter bilirubin from the blood, causing yellowing of skin and eyes.

qe: Which of the following prevents the entry of food into the windpipe (trachea) during swallowing?
e: The epiglottis is a cartilaginous flap that acts as a switch, covering the windpipe while swallowing to prevent choking.

qe: The 'Lacteals' found in the villi of the small intestine are responsible for the absorption of:
e: Lacteals are specialized lymphatic capillaries that absorb dietary fats (fatty acids and glycerol) that are too large for blood capillaries.

qe: What is the semi-solid mass of food called once it leaves the stomach and enters the small intestine?
e: Chyme is the thick, acidic fluid consisting of gastric juices and partly digested food. Bolus is what we swallow from the mouth.

qe: Which enzyme converts proteins into peptones and proteoses in the stomach?
e: Pepsin is the primary protein-digesting enzyme of the stomach, active only in a high-acid (low pH) environment.

qe: Which part of the Large Intestine hosts symbiotic bacteria that produce Vitamin K?
e: The cecum is a blind pouch that houses beneficial bacteria which aid in further digestion and vitamin synthesis.

qe: Severe protein deficiency in children, characterized by a 'pot belly' and thin limbs, is called:
e: Kwashiorkor is caused by sufficient calorie intake but severe protein deficiency. Marasmus is a deficiency of both calories and protein.

qe: Which cells of the gastric glands secrete 'Castle's Intrinsic Factor' for Vitamin B12 absorption?
e: Oxyntic cells secrete both HCl and Intrinsic Factor. Without this factor, Vitamin B12 cannot be absorbed, leading to anemia.

qe: The 'Islets of Langerhans' which produce insulin are located in which organ?
e: The pancreas is a dual-purpose gland; the Islets of Langerhans perform the endocrine function by secreting hormones like insulin and glucagon.

qe: Which digestive juice lacks enzymes but is essential for the digestion of fats?
e: Bile juice contains no enzymes. It contains bile salts that emulsify fats, breaking them into tiny droplets for lipase to act upon.

qe: Glands of Brunner (Duodenal glands) are found in which layer of the duodenum?
e: Brunner's glands are located in the sub-mucosa of the duodenum and secrete alkaline mucus to neutralize stomach acid.

qe: Which hormone triggers the contraction of the Gallbladder to release bile?
e: CCK is released by the small intestine when fats enter, signaling the gallbladder to squeeze bile into the duodenum.

qe: The 'Crypts of Lieberkuhn' are found in:
e: These are tubular glands found between the bases of the villi in the small intestine that secrete intestinal juice.

qe: Which of the following is an autoimmune disorder where the body attacks the lining of the small intestine due to gluten?
e: Celiac disease is a serious immune reaction to eating gluten, a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye.

qe: What is the main function of the Colon?
o: Preparation of feces and water absorption
e: The colon concentrates waste material by removing water and forming solid feces for elimination.

qe: Which enzyme converts Maltose into two molecules of Glucose?
e: Maltase is an intestinal enzyme that specifically breaks down the disaccharide maltose into simple glucose units.

qe: The wave-like muscular contractions that push food through the digestive tract are called:
e: Peristalsis is the involuntary contraction and relaxation of longitudinal and circular muscles throughout the gut.

qe: Which organ stores glycogen and helps in maintaining blood glucose levels?
e: The liver converts excess glucose into glycogen for storage (glycogenesis) and releases it back when blood sugar is low.

qe: What is the dental formula for milk teeth (deciduous teeth) in human children?
e: Children have 20 milk teeth. They lack premolars and the third molar (wisdom tooth). The formula is 2-1-0-2.

qe: Which of the following is the largest gland in the human body?
e: The liver is the largest gland, weighing about 1.5 kg in an adult. It performs over 500 vital functions.

qe: The 'Sphincter of Oddi' guards the opening of which duct?
e: The Sphincter of Oddi controls the flow of digestive juices (bile and pancreatic juice) into the duodenum.

qe: Which enzyme is NOT found in pancreatic juice?
e: Enterokinase is an intestinal enzyme that activates trypsinogen into trypsin. The others are pancreatic enzymes.

qe: Which part of the small intestine is the longest and highly coiled?
e: The Ileum is the final and longest segment of the small intestine, measuring about 3.5 meters.

qe: The condition 'Marasmus' is caused by the deficiency of:
e: Marasmus is severe malnutrition characterized by energy deficiency, affecting infants under one year.

qe: Which pigment gives the characteristic brown color to human feces?
e: Stercobilin is a biochemical catabolite of hemoglobin that provides the brown color to stool.

qe: The movement of water across the intestinal wall occurs by:
e: Water absorption in the intestines follows the osmotic gradient created by the absorption of nutrients and ions.

qe: Which part of the tooth is the hardest and lacks blood vessels?
e: Enamel is the most highly mineralized substance in the body and is non-living once formed.

qe: The secretion of 'Secretin' hormone is triggered by:
e: Acidic chyme entering the duodenum stimulates S-cells to release Secretin, which signals the pancreas to release bicarbonate.

qe: Which of the following is an example of mechanical digestion?
e: Mastication is the physical breakdown of food into smaller pieces by the teeth.

qe: Where are 'Peyer's Patches' (lymphoid tissue) located?
e: Peyer's patches are organized lymphoid follicles found in the submucosa of the small intestine, mainly the ileum.

qe: Which enzyme converts Chymotrypsinogen into active Chymotrypsin?
e: Once trypsin is activated by enterokinase, it goes on to activate chymotrypsinogen and procarboxypeptidase.

qe: The structural and functional unit of the liver is the:
e: Hepatic lobules are small, hexagonal functional units of the liver consisting of plates of hepatocytes.

qe: What is the function of the 'Serosa' layer in the alimentary canal?
e: The serosa is the outermost layer that secretes serous fluid to reduce friction during digestive movements.

qe: Absorption of alcohol and simple sugars starts in which organ?
e: While most nutrients are absorbed in the small intestine, alcohol and some drugs are absorbed directly through the stomach lining.

qe: Which of the following describes the human dentition?
e: Humans have teeth in sockets (Thecodont), two sets of teeth (Diphyodont), and different types of teeth (Heterodont).

qe: What is the primary site of fat digestion in the human body?
e: The small intestine receives bile for emulsification and pancreatic lipase for the final breakdown of fats.

qe: Which enzyme converts Milk into Curd in the human stomach (infants)?
e: Rennin (Chymosin) is secreted by gastric glands in infants to coagulate milk for better digestion.

qe: The hormone 'Secretin' is produced by which organ?
e: Secretin is produced by the S-cells of the duodenum to regulate the pH of the small intestine.

qe: Which mineral prevents 'Dental Caries' (tooth decay)?
e: Fluorine (as Fluoride) strengthens tooth enamel and makes it more resistant to acid attacks from bacteria.

qe: Which part of the digestive system has no digestive function?
e: The esophagus is a simple muscular tube that transports food via peristalsis without secreting enzymes.

qe: The maximum amount of energy is released by the oxidation of:
e: Fats provide roughly 9 kcal//gram, which is more than double the energy provided by carbs or proteins (4 kcal//gram).

qe: The 'G-cells' of the stomach secrete which hormone?
e: Gastrin stimulates the parietal cells to secrete Hydrochloric acid (HCl) for digestion.

qe: Which enzyme is responsible for the activation of Trypsinogen?
e: Enterokinase, secreted by the intestinal mucosa, converts inactive trypsinogen into active trypsin.

qe: Which part of the small intestine is the primary site for iron absorption?
e: Most dietary iron is absorbed in the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine.

qe: The 'Dental Formula' for a 17-year-old human (before wisdom teeth) is:
e: Before the third molars (wisdom teeth) erupt, the formula is 2-1-2-2.

qe: Which part of the tooth contains the 'Odontoblasts'?
e: Odontoblasts are cells in the dental pulp that produce dentine.

qe: The primary bile acids are synthesized from:
e: The liver converts cholesterol into primary bile acids like cholic acid.

qe: The 'Rugae' (folds) are found in the inner lining of which organ?
e: Rugae allow the stomach to expand significantly after a large meal.

qe: The 'Islets of Langerhans' contain Alpha cells that secrete which hormone?
e: Alpha cells secrete Glucagon (raises blood sugar), while Beta cells secrete Insulin (lowers blood sugar).

qe: The digestion of DNA and RNA is carried out by which pancreatic enzymes?
e: Nucleases (DNase and RNase) in the pancreatic juice break down nucleic acids into nucleotides.

qe: The 'Brunner's Glands' are found in which specific part of the small intestine?
e: Brunner's glands are unique to the duodenum and secrete alkaline mucus to protect against stomach acid.

qe: What is the common name for the 'Upper Esophageal Sphincter'?
e: The cricopharyngeal sphincter prevents air from entering the esophagus during breathing.

qe: Which mineral is required for the activation of the 'Salivary Amylase' enzyme?
e: Chloride ions (Cl-) act as activators for salivary amylase (ptyalin) in the mouth.

qe: The 'Hepatopancreatic ampulla' is also known as the:
e: The Ampulla of Vater is where the bile duct and the pancreatic duct join to enter the duodenum.

qe: What is the pH of Saliva in a healthy human?
e: Saliva is slightly acidic to neutral (average pH 6.8), which is ideal for the action of amylase.

qe: The process of 'Defecation' is controlled by which part of the Nervous System?
e: The involuntary part is parasympathetic, while the external anal sphincter is under voluntary (somatic) control.

qe: What is the average length of the 'Esophagus' in an adult human?
e: The esophagus is a muscular tube approximately 25 cm (10 inches) long.

qe: The reflex action of 'Vomiting' is controlled by the center located in which part of the brain?
e: The vomit center is located in the medulla oblongata, which regulates involuntary functions like breathing and heart rate.

qe: 'Constipation' is a digestive disorder primarily related to the malfunction of which organ?
e: In constipation, the feces are retained within the colon (large intestine) as the bowel movements occur irregularly.

qe: Which enzyme is deficient in a person suffering from 'Lactose Intolerance'?
e: Lactase is needed to break down lactose (milk sugar). Its deficiency causes bloating and diarrhea after consuming dairy.

qe: Which of the following is an example of an 'Exocrine' secretion of the Pancreas?
e: Pancreatic juice containing enzymes is an exocrine secretion released into ducts. Hormones like insulin are endocrine.

qe: The sensation of 'Heartburn' (Acid Reflux) is caused by the failure of which sphincter?
e: When the cardiac sphincter doesn't close properly, stomach acid flows back into the esophagus, causing a burning sensation.

qe: Which condition is characterized by the inability of the body to absorb nutrients, leading to weight loss?
e: Malabsorption syndrome occurs when the small intestine cannot adequately absorb nutrients like proteins, fats, and vitamins.

qe: The hormone 'Ghrelin', often called the 'Hunger Hormone', is primarily produced by:
e: Ghrelin is secreted by the stomach lining when it is empty, signaling the brain to increase appetite.

qe: Which digestive enzyme is active at the lowest (most acidic) pH?
e: Pepsin works optimally at a pH of around 1.5 to 2.0 in the stomach.

qe: The 'Haustra' are small pouches caused by sacculation, which give the ________ its segmented appearance.
e: Haustra are characteristic of the colon and are formed by the contraction of the taenia coli muscles.

qe: The 'Peyer's Patches' found in the ileum are a part of which system?
e: Peyer's patches are lymphoid follicles that monitor bacterial populations and prevent the growth of pathogenic bacteria in the intestines.

qe: The movement of food in the esophagus is regulated by which type of muscle?
e: The upper third of the esophagus is skeletal (voluntary), while the lower two-thirds are smooth muscle (involuntary).

qe: Which of the following is NOT a part of the 'Large Intestine'?
e: The Duodenum is the first part of the small intestine. The large intestine consists of the caecum, colon, and rectum.

qe: What is the function of the 'Gallbladder'?
e: The liver produces bile, but the gallbladder stores it and removes water to make it more concentrated for fat digestion.

qe: Which of the following describes the pH of the Small Intestine?
e: Bicarbonate from the pancreas neutralizes stomach acid, making the small intestine slightly alkaline (pH 7.5 - 8.5).

qe: The condition where the body cannot properly digest 'Gluten' is called:
e: Celiac disease is an immune reaction to eating gluten, which damages the lining of the small intestine.

qe: Which enzyme converts 'Proteoses and Peptones' into Dipeptides in the small intestine?
e: Pancreatic enzymes like trypsin and chymotrypsin continue the protein digestion started in the stomach.

qe: Which of the following is a function of the 'Large Intestine'?
e: The colon primarily recovers water and electrolytes from the waste material before it is expelled.

qe: What is the role of 'Bile Salts' in digestion?
e: Bile salts break down large fat globules into tiny micelles, increasing the surface area for lipase to work.

qe: Which of the following vitamins is primarily absorbed in the 'Ileum'?
e: Vitamin B12 absorption requires intrinsic factor from the stomach and takes place specifically in the terminal ileum.

qe: What is the common passage for the 'Bile duct' and the 'Pancreatic duct'?
e: These two ducts join to form the common hepatopancreatic duct, which opens into the duodenum.

qe: Which enzyme converts 'Dipeptides' into 'Amino Acids'?
e: Dipeptidases are part of the intestinal juice (succus entericus) that complete the final step of protein digestion.

qe: What is 'Deglutition'?
e: Deglutition is the medical term for the act of swallowing food or liquid.

qe: Which part of the teeth contains the blood vessels and nerves?
e: The pulp cavity is the soft center of the tooth that contains living tissue, providing sensation and nourishment.

qe: Which of the following is the inactive precursor of the enzyme 'Pepsin'?
e: Pepsinogen is the zymogen (inactive form) secreted by chief cells. It is converted to active pepsin by stomach acid (HCl).

qe: Which hormone causes the secretion of bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice?
e: Secretin is released by the duodenum in response to acid. It stimulates the pancreas to release water and bicarbonate to neutralize the acid.

qe: Which of the following is a 'Polysaccharide' that humans cannot digest but acts as roughage?
e: Humans lack the enzyme cellulase. Cellulose stays in the gut and helps in the smooth movement of feces.

qe: Which part of the teeth is the most mineralized and hardest part?
e: Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body, containing 96% mineral content.

qe: Which valve prevents the backflow of fecal matter from the large intestine into the small intestine?
e: The ileocaecal valve connects the ileum to the caecum and is a one-way door.

qe: What is the primary function of the 'Gallbladder'?
e: Bile is made by the liver. The gallbladder removes water to make the bile more potent for fat digestion.

qe: Which cells of the stomach secrete 'Intrinsic Factor' essential for Vitamin B12 absorption?
e: Parietal cells secrete both HCl and Intrinsic Factor. Deficiency leads to pernicious anemia.

qe: What is the 'pH' of the Succus Entericus (Intestinal Juice)?
e: Intestinal juice is slightly alkaline (pH 7.8) to facilitate enzyme activity in the small intestine.

qe: The protein digesting enzyme found in the 'Pancreatic Juice' is:
e: Trypsin, Chymotrypsin, and Carboxypeptidase are the protein enzymes from the pancreas.

qe: The yellow pigment 'Bilirubin' is formed from the breakdown of:
e: Old red blood cells are broken down in the spleen and liver, producing bilirubin as a waste product.

qe: Which enzyme converts 'Dipeptides' into individual 'Amino acids'?
e: Dipeptidases are part of the intestinal juice (Succus Entericus) and perform the final step of protein digestion.

qe: A 'Balanced Diet' for an adult should typically consist of carbs, proteins, and fats in what ratio?
e: The general recommendation is roughly 4 parts carbohydrates to 1 part protein and 1 part fat.

qe: The 'Islets of Langerhans' secrete Insulin from which specific cells?
e: Beta cells produce insulin. Alpha cells produce glucagon.

qe: The 'Dental Formula' for a human child (milk teeth) is:
e: Children lack premolars and the third molar. The formula is 2-1-0-2.

qe: The 'Large Intestine' lacks which of the following structures found in the small intestine?
e: Villi are for absorption of nutrients. Since nutrient absorption is mostly finished, the large intestine does not have villi.

qe: Which disorder is characterized by the accumulation of 'Uric Acid' crystals in joints?
e: While not purely digestive, Gout is linked to the diet and metabolic breakdown of purines.

qe: The common bile duct is formed by the union of:
e: The cystic duct (from gallbladder) and hepatic duct (from liver) join to form the common bile duct.

qe: Which mineral is required for the 'Coagulation' of blood?
e: Calcium ions are essential for the conversion of prothrombin to thrombin.

qe: What is the lifespan of a 'Red Blood Cell' (RBC)?
e: After about 120 days, RBCs are broken down in the spleen and liver.

qe: The 'Glycemic Index' (GI) is a measure of how quickly ________ increase blood glucose levels.
e: High-GI foods like white bread cause a rapid spike in blood sugar, while low-GI foods release energy slowly.

qe: Which part of the digestive system is responsible for the 'Enterohepatic circulation' of bile salts?
e: About 95% of bile salts are reabsorbed in the terminal ileum and returned to the liver via the portal vein.

qe: Which enzyme converts 'Lactose' (milk sugar) into Glucose and Galactose?
e: Lactase is found on the brush border of the small intestine. Its absence leads to lactose intolerance.

qe: Which specific cells in the stomach secrete 'Mucus' to protect the lining from acid?
e: Mucus forms a physical barrier that prevents the HCl from digesting the stomach's own wall.

qe: What is 'Steatorrhea'?
e: Steatorrhea occurs when fats are not properly digested or absorbed, often due to a lack of bile or lipase.

qe: Which part of the Alimentary Canal is missing 'Serosa' and instead has 'Adventitia'?
e: The esophagus lacks a serosal layer; its outer layer is fibrous connective tissue called adventitia.

qe: What is the 'Specific Dynamic Action' (SDA) of food?
o: Energy used for digestion and metabolism
e: SDA is the amount of energy expenditure above the basal metabolic rate due to the cost of processing food for use and storage.

qe: Which of the following is a 'Micronutrient' essential for bone health?
e: Calcium is a mineral (micronutrient) that provides structural integrity to bones and teeth.

qe: What is 'Deglutition Apnea'?
o: Temporary stoppage of breathing during swallowing
e: The respiratory center in the brain is inhibited during swallowing to prevent food from entering the lungs.

qe: Which hormone stimulates the 'Pancreas' to release digestive enzymes (not bicarbonate)?
e: CCK stimulates the secretion of enzyme-rich pancreatic juice, while Secretin stimulates water and bicarbonate release.

qe: The 'Taeniae Coli' are three bands of longitudinal smooth muscle found in the:
e: These muscles cause the colon to pucker into small pouches called haustra.

qe: Which of the following describes the role of 'Gastric Lipase'?
o: Minor digestion of fats in the stomach
e: Gastric lipase initiates a small amount of fat digestion, but 90% happens in the small intestine.

qe: The 'Pylorus' is the opening between the:
e: The pyloric sphincter controls the flow of chyme into the small intestine.

qe: Which vitamin deficiency causes 'Glossitis' (inflammation of the tongue)?
e: B-complex deficiencies often manifest as oral health issues like glossitis or cheilosis.

qe: Which of the following is NOT a salivary gland?
e: Adrenal glands are part of the endocrine system and located on top of the kidneys.

qe: What is the function of 'Bicarbonate' in pancreatic juice?
e: It creates the alkaline environment necessary for intestinal enzymes to function.

qe: Which condition results from the failure of the liver to remove 'Bile pigments' from the blood?
e: Excess bilirubin causes the yellowing of skin and eyes known as jaundice.

qe: The primary site for the absorption of 'Fat-soluble vitamins' (A, D, E, K) is:
e: Absorption occurs in the small intestine alongside dietary fats via micelles.

qe: Which enzyme converts 'Sucrose' into Glucose and Fructose?
e: Sucrase is produced by the small intestine to break down table sugar (sucrose).

qe: Which hormone is known as the 'Hunger Hormone'?
e: Ghrelin is produced by the stomach and signals the brain that it's time to eat.

qe: What is the role of 'Gastric Inhibitory Peptide' (GIP)?
e: GIP is released when fats and sugars enter the duodenum; it slows the stomach down to allow for proper absorption.

qe: The 'Crypts of Lieberkühn' secrete which of the following?
e: These are tubular glands in the intestinal lining that produce 'Succus Entericus' (intestinal juice).

qe: Which vitamin is synthesized by 'Colonic bacteria' in the human body?
e: Bacteria like E. coli in the large intestine produce Vitamin K and some B-complex vitamins as a byproduct of fermentation.

qe: The 'Enteric Nervous System' is often referred to as the:
e: The gut has its own independent network of neurons that can control digestion even without signals from the brain.

qe: Which of the following is an 'Essential Amino Acid' that must be obtained from diet?
e: Lysine is one of the 9 essential amino acids that the human body cannot synthesize on its own.

qe: What is the function of 'Bile Pigments' (Bilirubin and Biliverdin)?
e: Bile pigments are waste products of hemoglobin breakdown and do not play a role in digestion.

qe: A deficiency of 'Fluorine' in drinking water primarily leads to:
e: Fluoride is essential for strengthening tooth enamel; its lack leads to tooth decay (caries).

qe: What is the primary site of 'Alcohol' absorption in the human body?
e: While some absorption happens in the intestine, alcohol is unique because it can be absorbed directly through the stomach lining.

qe: The 'Haustra' are characteristic pouches found in which organ?
e: Haustra are small pouches caused by sacculation, which give the colon its segmented appearance.

qe: Which hormone stimulates the 'Gallbladder' to contract and release bile?
e: CCK is secreted by the duodenum in response to fats; it triggers gallbladder contraction and pancreatic enzyme release.

qe: What is the primary function of the 'Kupffer Cells' in the liver?
e: Kupffer cells are specialized macrophages that destroy bacteria and old red blood cells in the liver.

qe: Which of the following describes 'Micelles' in the digestive process?
o: Small droplets of fats surrounded by bile salts
e: Micelles are essential for the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins and fatty acids in the small intestine.

qe: Which enzyme converts 'Maltose' into two units of 'Glucose'?
e: Maltase is an intestinal enzyme that completes the digestion of malt sugar into simple glucose.

qe: What is 'Achalasia'?
o: Failure of the lower esophageal sphincter to relax
e: Achalasia makes it difficult for food and liquid to pass from the esophagus into the stomach.

qe: Which part of the Alimentary canal is the site of 'Symbiotic bacteria' that produce Vitamin K?
e: The caecum and colon host beneficial bacteria like E. coli which synthesize Vitamin K and B12.

qe: The 'Islets of Langerhans' are found in which organ?
e: These are groups of endocrine cells in the pancreas that secrete insulin and glucagon.

qe: What is 'Peristalsis'?
o: Wave-like muscular contractions of the gut
e: Peristalsis pushes food through the esophagus, stomach, and intestines involuntarily.

qe: Which enzyme converts 'Proteins' into 'Amino Acids' in the small intestine?
e: Peptidases (from intestinal juice) perform the final step of breaking down small peptides into individual amino acids.

qe: Which condition is caused by the lack of 'Intrinsic Factor' in the stomach?
e: Without intrinsic factor, Vitamin B12 cannot be absorbed, leading to failure of RBC maturation.

qe: The 'Splanchnic Circulation' refers to the blood flow of which system?
e: It includes the blood flow to the stomach, intestines, liver, spleen, and pancreas.

qe: What is the primary function of the 'Ileocaecal Valve'?
o: Prevent backflow from Large Intestine to Small Intestine
e: It acts as a one-way door to ensure waste material does not move back into the nutrient-absorbing small intestine.

qe: The 'Auerbach's Plexus' (Myenteric Plexus) primarily controls:
e: Located between the muscle layers of the gut, it regulates the speed and strength of peristalsis.

qe: What is 'Achalasia Cardia'?
o: Failure of the lower esophageal sphincter to relax
e: It makes it difficult for food to enter the stomach, often causing the esophagus to dilate.

qe: Which of the following is an 'Incisor' tooth function?
e: Incisors are the chisel-shaped front teeth used specifically for biting and cutting.

qe: Which hormone is secreted by the 'Delta Cells' of the Pancreas?
e: Somatostatin inhibits the secretion of both insulin and glucagon to maintain balance.

qe: What is the function of 'Bicarbonate Ions' in saliva?
o: Buffer and neutralize acids from bacteria
e: Bicarbonate helps protect tooth enamel by neutralizing acids produced by oral bacteria.

qe: The 'Meissner's Plexus' is located in which layer of the gut wall?
e: The sub-mucosal plexus primarily regulates secretions and local blood flow.

qe: Which digestive juice is the most 'Enzyme-rich'?
e: Pancreatic juice contains enzymes for digesting all three major food types: carbs, proteins, and fats.

qe: What is 'Borborygmi'?
e: It is the sound of gas and fluid moving through the intestines.

qe: Which part of the 'Large Intestine' acts as a temporary storage for feces?
e: The rectum holds waste until the stretch receptors trigger the urge to defecate.

qe: Which enzyme converts 'Polypeptides' into 'Dipeptides'?
e: Chymotrypsin is a pancreatic enzyme that continues the protein breakdown started in the stomach.

qe: Which of the following is a 'Symbiotic' organism found in the human gut?
e: E. coli helps synthesize Vitamin K and prevents the growth of harmful bacteria.

qe: What is the 'Normal Flora' of the digestive tract?
e: It refers to the trillion of microbes that live in the gut and aid in immunity and digestion.

qe: Which of the following is an example of an 'Accessory Organ' of digestion?
e: Accessory organs like the liver and pancreas are not part of the 'tube' but secrete essential juices into it.

qe: What is 'Steatorrhea' primarily a symptom of?
e: Steatorrhea is the presence of excess fat in feces, often due to a lack of bile or pancreatic lipase.

qe: Which part of the stomach is closest to the opening of the esophagus?
e: The cardia is the region where the esophagus enters the stomach, protected by the cardiac sphincter.

qe: What is the 'pH' of the duodenum after the mixing of acidic chyme and alkaline juices?
e: Bicarbonate from the pancreas neutralizes the acid, raising the pH to slightly alkaline (7.0-8.5).

qe: Which condition is caused by the autoimmune destruction of the 'Parietal Cells'?
e: Parietal cells produce Intrinsic Factor; their destruction prevents Vitamin B12 absorption.

qe: What is the 'Vagus Nerve's' (Cranial Nerve X) role in the digestive system?
e: The Vagus nerve stimulates gastric acid secretion, enzyme release, and gut motility.

qe: The 'Taeniae Coli' are characteristic longitudinal muscle bands found in the:
e: These three bands of smooth muscle cause the large intestine to pucker into pouches called haustra.

qe: Which enzyme converts 'Dipeptides' into individual 'Amino Acids'?
e: Dipeptidases are part of the intestinal juice (Succus Entericus) and finish the last step of protein digestion.

qe: The hormone 'Ghrelin' is primarily produced in the ________ to signal hunger.
e: Ghrelin is secreted by the stomach lining and increases appetite by acting on the brain.

qe: What is the primary role of 'Bile Salts' in digestion?
e: Bile salts break down large fat globules into tiny droplets, increasing the surface area for lipase.

qe: Which cell in the liver is responsible for 'Detoxification' of alcohol and drugs?
e: Hepatocytes (liver cells) contain abundant Smooth ER that processes and neutralizes toxins.

qe: What is the 'Specific Dynamic Action' (SDA) of protein-rich food?
e: Proteins have the highest SDA, meaning about 30% of their energy is consumed just to digest and process them.

qe: Which enzyme converts 'Polynucleotides' into 'Nucleotides' in the small intestine?
e: Pancreatic nucleases (DNase and RNase) break down DNA and RNA from food into their basic building blocks.

qe: Which of the following is a 'Polysaccharide' that cannot be digested by humans?
e: Humans lack the enzyme cellulase. Cellulose acts as dietary fiber to help move waste through the gut.

qe: Which hormone is known as the 'Brake of the Stomach' as it slows down gastric emptying?
e: GIP inhibits gastric secretion and motility to allow the duodenum time to process fats and sugars.

qe: Which organ in the human body is the primary site for 'Gluconeogenesis'?
e: The liver can synthesize glucose from non-carbohydrate sources like amino acids during fasting.

qe: Which vitamin is essential for the synthesis of 'Prothrombin' for blood clotting?
e: Vitamin K is a co-factor for the liver enzymes that produce clotting factors.

qe: The 'Sphincter of Oddi' regulates the flow of juice into the:
e: It guards the hepatopancreatic ampulla opening into the first part of the small intestine.

qe: Which mineral is required for the activation of 'Salivary Amylase'?
e: Chloride ions (Cl-) act as activators for the starch-digesting enzyme in the mouth.

qe: Why does 'Acute Pancreatitis' lead to the organ digesting itself?
o: Premature activation of Trypsinogen inside the pancreas
e: Normally, trypsin is activated only in the duodenum. If it activates inside the pancreas, it starts a chain reaction that digests the organ's own proteins.

qe: Which hormone is responsible for 'Autonomy of the Gut' (The Second Brain)?
e: The Enteric Nervous System uses Acetylcholine and other neurotransmitters to manage digestion even if the brain connection is severed.

qe: Which specific cell in the stomach is responsible for 'Pernicious Anemia' if it fails?
e: Parietal cells produce Intrinsic Factor. Without it, Vitamin B12 cannot be absorbed, stopping RBC production.

qe: Which digestive process is primarily 'Mechanical' rather than chemical?
e: Bile salts do not break chemical bonds; they act like soap to physically break large fat drops into tiny ones.

qe: What is the function of 'Enterogastrone' released by the duodenum?
e: It acts as a 'brake' to slow down the stomach when the small intestine is full of fats.

qe: The 'Gastro-colic reflex' is responsible for:
e: Stretching the stomach signals the colon to move its contents, often leading to a bowel movement after a meal.

qe: Which part of the teeth is 'Living' and contains nerves?
e: The pulp cavity is the soft, living center of the tooth. Enamel and Dentine are non-living mineral layers.

qe: The 'Chyle' is different from 'Chyme' because it contains:
e: Chyme is in the stomach; Chyle is the milky fluid in the small intestine containing absorbed fats.

qe: Why is the 'Terminal Ileum' so important in the digestive postmortem?
o: It is the only site for Vitamin B12 and Bile Salt reabsorption
e: If the terminal ileum is damaged, the body cannot recycle bile or absorb B12, leading to severe malnutrition.

qe: Which of the following is the 'Hardest' substance in the human body?
e: Tooth enamel is the most mineralized and hardest tissue in the body.

qe: What is the 'pH' of the Small Intestine after the addition of pancreatic juice?
e: Bicarbonate in pancreatic juice neutralizes stomach acid, raising the pH to around 8.0 for enzyme activity.

qe: Which hormone inhibits 'Gastric motility' when the small intestine is full?
e: GIP signals the stomach to slow down so the intestine doesn't get overwhelmed.

qe: An infection of the 'Parotid Glands' by a virus results in which disease?
e: Mumps is a viral infection that primarily affects the parotid salivary glands located near the ears.

qe: Which hormone inhibits gastric secretion and motility?
e: Gastric Inhibitory Peptide (GIP) slows down the stomach to allow the intestine time to process fats.

qe: What is the common name for the third molar teeth in humans?
e: Wisdom teeth are the last set of molars to erupt, usually between ages 17 and 25.

qe: Which part of the Alimentary canal is the widest?
e: The stomach is a J-shaped, sac-like organ that is the widest part of the digestive tract.

qe: Which vitamin is synthesized by bacteria in the human colon?
e: E. coli and other bacteria in the large intestine produce Vitamin K and some B-complex vitamins.

qe: An abnormal frequency of bowel movement and increased liquidity of fecal discharge is:
e: Diarrhea reduces the absorption of food and can lead to severe dehydration.
